t: You ate. I can see that much from here.
Your stomach is quiet while mine has not stopped all day.
Do not speak to me about patience with food in you.
I have watched you work without once wondering where supper went.
One of us was fed today. It was not me.
You look comfortable enough. I can barely think straight.
{god} provided for you. Did the rest of us escape notice?
You give thanks with a full belly while I wait for mine.
Maybe {god} chose who ate. That thought is not helping me.
I keep asking whether this is chance. You keep looking well fed.
No god divided the food this badly. People did.
Prayer filled your mouth sooner than it filled mine.
If you are going to watch me eat, at least say what you mean.
I did not decide that you would go hungry today.
That look will not put food in either hand.
You have blamed me since noticing I had eaten.
I know you are hungry. I do not know why that makes me guilty.
Say what you want from me instead of staring at my stomach.
{god} gave me food, not the right to decide your share.
I thanked {god} for eating. I did not ask that you go without.
Maybe I was fortunate. That does not make your hunger my choice.
I wondered why I ate and you did not. I have no answer.
The stores failed you, not me. Aim your anger somewhere useful.
Do not turn unequal portions into another lesson about {god}.
You can explain after you have missed as many meals as I have.
I did ask. Empty hands were the answer.
You say it was not your choice as though that feeds me.
I am not blaming your stomach. I am blaming your indifference.
Then help me find food instead of defending yourself.
You noticed the difference and kept walking. That was a choice.
{god} asks us to share what we receive. You heard that too.
Providence means little if the fed refuse to look at the hungry.
Perhaps nobody chose this. Somebody can still choose to help now.
I do not know whom to blame. You are the one answering me.
Good. Leave {god} out of it and tell me where the food went.
I asked people for food before I wasted breath asking heaven.
I ate what was given to me. I took nothing from you.
You think I have food hidden because I am not hungry now.
I cannot return a meal already eaten. Tell me what would help next.
Being fed today does not mean I have never gone without.
I did not see you waiting. I would have said something.
I am listening now. Stop speaking as though I emptied the stores.
{god}'s gift was not mine to refuse out of shame.
I will ask {god} for your meal as firmly as I asked for mine.
Maybe I should have asked who remained hungry. I did not think.
I cannot explain why I was fed. I can admit it feels unfair.
Exactly. People failed to divide it fairly. I am only one person.
Blame the hands that counted the portions, not an invisible judge.
You keep explaining the meal while my stomach keeps answering.
I should not have to beg a neighbor who can see the difference.
If you truly did not notice, look at me now.
I am tired of being reasonable on an empty stomach.
Find me when you have something useful, not another excuse.
Perhaps I chose the wrong person to confront. You were simply nearest.
{god} sees both stomachs. I am waiting to see what you do.
Keep defending your portion. {god} heard every word.
Maybe I am blaming you because I cannot argue with chance.
I want this to mean something. Mostly, I want supper.
There is no lesson here. One person ate and another did not.
Save the prayers. Help me find an honest portion.
I cannot make myself hungry enough to satisfy you.
You want me ashamed when what you need is food.
I offered to help. I will not accept blame for everything before that.
I see the difference. I resent being treated as its cause.
Keep shouting if you like. It will not refill the sacks.
I should have noticed sooner. That is the fault I will admit.
{god} gave enough for one meal. I cannot make it two.
I will pray and work for more. I will not apologize for eating.
Perhaps fortune should embarrass me more than it does.
I do not know why I ate first. I know this argument solves nothing.
If you want fairness, speak to the people dividing the stores.
{god} did not fill my bowl. Someone with a ladle did.
I am leaving before hunger makes me say worse.
Keep your explanation. I need to find something to eat.
I should not have blamed you for all of it. Not all of it.
Next time you eat, look around before taking the last mouthful.
Do not follow me unless you know where food is.
I spoke badly. The hunger remains, but that part was mine.
I will take this complaint to the shrine and leave you out of it.
{god} will judge whether a full stomach excused that answer.
Perhaps nobody intended this. I still cannot stand beside you now.
I need food before I decide whether I owe you an apology.
I will ask people with food instead of people with explanations.
There is nothing divine here worth discussing. I am going.
I will ask around for food. That is all I can offer now.
I am sorry you went without. I am not sorry that I ate.
Come find me later. We can look through the stores together.
I have heard enough blame for one meal. I am leaving.
Next time I see you waiting, I will speak up.
You deserved food. You did not deserve to accuse me of taking it.
I will pray that both of us eat tomorrow. That is sincere.
May {god} feed you soon and soften both our words.
I might owe you more than an explanation. Let me think.
I was fortunate and defensive. Both can be true.
Find the person who divided the portions. I will come with you.
I will help find food. I will not pretend heaven chose my meal.
